_comment: COUPLING tier-2. The comparative half of the accelerator advice — 'Measured across conductance ratios rho from 1/4 to 9 ... Aitken matched or beat a constant theta almost everywhere, and in a quarter of those settings it converged to the right interface value where the SAME constant theta diverged by tens of orders of magnitude'. Reproducing a sweep is not what a fixture is for; this takes ONE strongly unbalanced ratio and the one theta the knowledge itself hands an agent who cannot estimate rho ('first try, cannot estimate rho at all: theta=0.5, keep accelerator=aitken') and races the two accelerators against the closed form under an IDENTICAL max_iter and tol, read back from each run rather than assumed. rho = 6 and not 9 for two measured reasons: theta=0.5 has to sit above the constant stability limit 2/(1+rho), which needs rho > 3, and the ratio has to be one the default actually recovers — at rho = 9 with theta = 0.5 the default DIVERGES too on this driver, by many orders of magnitude, just far fewer than the constant arm's, which is exactly the knowledge's own caveat that no accelerator rescues a badly split interface and why the comparative claim is worded 'almost everywhere'. The fixture asserts its own premise first (the naive theta must be above the limit at this ratio, arithmetic on the knowledge's formula before anything runs), then requires the default to land on the analytic interface temperature AND flux from both sides with the conservation balance and an empty validation block, and requires the constant arm to have MISSED that same check — a single success would not be a comparison. ||| KNOWN RED ON THE MERGED TREE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT RETUNED. This fixture passes on knowledge/coupling-revision and fails here, missing aitken_reached_closed_form=True and aitken_beat_constant=True. The cause is not this fixture: feature/coupling-robustness replaced the PER-PARTICIPANT Aitken theta with ONE global theta for the whole interface state (measured on the merged driver: 199 calls to _aitken over 200 iterations with two participants, where per-participant gives 398), and the global one no longer rescues a strongly unbalanced split at theta=0.5. The same effect was measured independently at rho=4 on the skfem conduction pair: aitken stalls at 3.7e-03 while a constant theta=0.2 converges in 83 iterations. IT IS LEFT FAILING ON PURPOSE. Moving RHO to a ratio where the default still wins would be choosing the setting that makes the served sentence true instead of measuring whether it is, and the served sentence — the 40-cell rho x theta sweep quoted in this fixture's docstring — was run on the per-participant accelerator, which no longer exists. Two of its cells have now been re-measured on the merged driver and neither reproduces. The outstanding work is to re-run that sweep and rewrite the claim from it; until then this red is the honest state and is recorded in docs/CONSOLIDATION.md.

_mutation.note: Move the ratio to a balanced one, where theta=0.5 IS 1/(1+rho) and therefore already the optimum. The advantage vanishes and the fixture fails three ways: the premise assertion fires because 0.5 is now below the stability limit 2/(1+rho)=1.0, the constant arm reaches the closed form so constant_reached_closed_form prints True, and aitken_beat_constant prints False. This is the mutation that matters for a COMPARATIVE claim — it does not break either accelerator, it removes the imbalance the claim is about, and only a fixture that picked a ratio where the naive theta is genuinely bad notices.
